title: Guardrails
subtitle: Check prompts and responses for personal data, injection attempts, leaked secrets, and your own rules. Companies, departments, projects, and API keys can change single parts.
companySubtitle: Give this company, its departments, projects, or API keys their own settings. Everything they leave open follows the platform policy.

overrides.title: Overrides
overrides.hint: An override changes single parts of the policy for one company, department, project, or API key. Parts it leaves open keep following the level above, from the API key up to the platform.
overrides.emptyHint: Every request follows the platform policy. Add an override to give a company, department, project, or API key its own settings for any part.
overrides.removeConfirmHint: Every part then follows the level above again.
overrides.noMatchesHint: Try another name, or clear the search.

dialog.hint: Pick who it applies to, then switch on the parts that should differ. You can save after any step.

dialog.clearing: No part is set here anymore, so saving removes the override.

pii.hint: Applies to every request unless its API key, project, department, or company sets personal data itself. Request logs always keep personal data masked.

pii.stepHint: {step, select, types {Choose the kinds of personal data to look for. Without a selection, the default set applies.} detection {Patterns find structured values. A redaction model also finds names and addresses in free text.} other {}}

enableHint: Covers text in every API call and in the playground. Uploaded files and audio are not scanned.
modeOption: {mode, select, mask {Mask} block {Block} restore {Mask and restore} other {{mode}}}
modeHint: {mode, select, mask {Replace each value with a placeholder such as [EMAIL_1]. The model never sees it.} block {Reject the request with error 400 before it reaches the model.} restore {Send placeholders to the model, then put the real values back into the answer.} other {}}
modeNote: Secrets and keys are always masked and never restored.
outputHint: Masks new personal data in the model's answer before the client sees it.
detectorOption: {detector, select, patterns {Patterns} model {Redaction model} both {Model and patterns} other {{detector}}}
detectorHint: {detector, select, patterns {Fixed rules find structured values such as email addresses, card numbers, and IDs.} model {The redaction model finds names, addresses, and other personal data in free text. Secrets and credentials are always caught by patterns first.} both {The redaction model and the patterns both run, and overlapping matches count once. Secrets and credentials are always caught by patterns first.} other {}}

failureOption: {failure, select, patterns {Fall back to patterns} block {Block the request (503)} other {{failure}}}
failureHint: Fallback redacts with patterns and logs a warning without request content. Block rejects the request with 503 pii_detector_unavailable.

model.title: Redaction model
model.description: Used by every policy whose detection includes the model, overrides included. Secrets never reach it.
model.label: Model
model.hint: {configured, select, true {LLMHUB_REDACTOR_URL provides the pii-tracer alias.} other {Pick an internal alias that speaks the token classification protocol, or set LLMHUB_REDACTOR_URL.}}
model.timeoutHint: Per request. When it runs out, the failure setting applies.
model.language: PII-Tracer documents English. Its model card does not state German coverage, so test German samples here before you rely on it, and prefer Model and patterns for structured IDs.
model.testerHint: Sends the sample to the selected model and lists the spans it finds. Nothing is stored.
